title: Communication-Efficient Distributed Statistical Inference
authors: Jordan, Michael I.; Lee, Jason D.; Yang, Yun
venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association 114(526)
summary: Introduces a surrogate likelihood that uses the full local data of one machine plus gradients from the others, so a few communication rounds give an estimator that beats simple averaging and supports confidence intervals and a quasi-posterior. Also gives a minimax-optimal regularised version for high dimensions; this is the standard reference for communication-efficient, near-pooled estimation.
verified_from: Crossref (bibliographic); abstract from arXiv abs page 1605.07689
note: JASA vol 114 (2019), online 2018. Full text read from arXiv 1605.07689 (abstract, discussion, targeted passages); abstract in record taken from the arXiv page.

title: Distributed testing and estimation under sparse high dimensional models
authors: Battey, Heather; Fan, Jianqing; Liu, Han; Lu, Junwei; Zhu, Ziwei
summary: Studies divide-and-conquer testing and estimation: aggregates statistics from k subsamples of size n/k and asks how many subsamples can be used before the aggregate loses the efficiency of the full-sample estimator, in low-dimensional and sparse high-dimensional models. Gives the conditions on k and proposes new test statistics and estimators.
note: Seed 'Battey et al. 2018'; confirmed as Battey, Fan, Liu, Lu, Zhu, Ann Stat 46(4).

title: Distributed linear regression by averaging
authors: Dobriban, Edgar; Sheng, Yue
summary: Analyses one-step and iterative weighted averaging of per-machine linear or ridge regressions when the number of parameters is comparable to the sample size, using random-matrix calculus. Finds that estimation error and confidence-interval length inflate considerably under averaging while prediction error rises much less.
note: Seed 'Dobriban and Sheng 2021'. Preprint arXiv 1810.00412 (full text retrieved and skimmed: abstract, simulation and conclusion). Relevant because the HEST head is a high-dimensional ridge and prediction error is the project's target.

title: WONDER: Weighted one-shot distributed ridge regression in high dimensions
authors: Dobriban, Edgar; Sheng, Yue
venue: arXiv preprint (ICML 2020 and JMLR 21 versions exist)
summary: Studies one-shot weighted combinations of local ridge estimators in a high-dimensional random-effects model and proposes the WONDER weights; reports that the optimal weights sum to more than one because ridge shrinks downward. On the Million Song data, the distributed fit saves at least 100-fold computation while nearly preserving test accuracy.
note: Same work as the ICML 2020 paper (PMLR v119 sheng20a) and JMLR 21 (2020) (the JMLR page was seen in a web result, so that venue is secondary). Averaging of local ridge fits, which differs from exact sufficient-statistic ridge.

title: Communication-Efficient Accurate Statistical Estimation
authors: Fan, Jianqing; Guo, Yongyi; Wang, Kaizheng
venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association 118(542)
summary: Proposes two iterative distributed estimators (CEASE) that adapt to the similarity of node loss functions and converge linearly, reaching full-sample statistical efficiency in a finite number of steps. Seed 'Fan, Guo and Wang 2023' (JASA 118(542):1000-1010; online 2021).
note: Preprint arXiv 1906.04870 retrieved to fedlearn_papers but only the abstract was read closely.

title: Communication-efficient sparse regression: a one-shot approach
authors: Lee, Jason D.; Sun, Yuekai; Liu, Qiang; Taylor, Jonathan E.
summary: Gives a one-shot distributed estimator for high-dimensional sparse regression by averaging debiased lasso estimates, with the lasso rate retained provided the data are not split across too many machines. Extends to generalised linear models.
note: Published later in JMLR per my recollection; not verified on a page opened here, so listed as preprint.

title: Communication-Efficient Algorithms for Statistical Optimization
authors: Zhang, Yuchen; Duchi, John C.; Wainwright, Martin
summary: Analyses averaging of local estimates and a bootstrap-bias-corrected variant for large-scale statistical optimisation, showing that averaging attains the full-sample rate when each machine holds enough data. A foundational reference for one-shot averaging.
note: Dated 2012; within T4's range (back to 2000) and a direct basis for the later included distributed-estimation papers. arXiv comment says to appear in JMLR. The arXiv page title spells 'Comunication'; corrected here.

title: Improved Distributed Principal Component Analysis
authors: Balcan, Maria-Florina; Kanchanapally, Vandana; Liang, Yingyu; Woodruff, David
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 27 (NeurIPS 2014)
summary: Gives a communication-efficient distributed PCA with provable approximation guarantees for the union of points held on several servers. Foundation for any federated basis of principal components.
verified_from: arXiv abs page 1408.5823; NeurIPS proceedings page https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2014/hash/e968f1646c1c6c35422b64c0934772a4-Abstract.html
note: Dated 2014; within T4's range (back to 2000). NeurIPS 2014 venue confirmed from the proceedings.neurips.cc page (opened); arXiv abs page also read. Abstract only.

title: Distributed estimation of principal eigenspaces
authors: Fan, Jianqing; Wang, Dong; Wang, Kaizheng; Zhu, Ziwei
summary: Each node sends its top eigenvectors and the centre runs PCA on the pooled eigenspaces; the paper derives the convergence rate and shows it matches whole-sample PCA when the number of machines is not too large. Extends to nodes with different population covariances.
note: Preprint arXiv 1702.06488 (full text retrieved, abstract and discussion read). Approximate aggregation; an exact PCA basis would instead follow from summed second moments, which this paper does not address.

title: Federated Principal Component Analysis
authors: Grammenos, Andreas; Mendoza-Smith, Rodrigo; Crowcroft, Jon; Mascolo, Cecilia
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33 (NeurIPS 2020)
summary: Presents a streaming, asynchronous, differentially private federated PCA that needs little memory and is invariant to the order in which nodes report. Simulations show it matches or beats non-federated memory-limited baselines.
verified_from: arXiv abs page 1907.08059; NeurIPS proceedings page proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2020/hash/47a658229eb2368a99f1d032c8848542
note: NeurIPS 2020, verified at proceedings.neurips.cc (page read). Full text of arXiv 1907.08059 retrieved; abstract and conclusion read. Evaluation uses MNIST and Wine only.

title: Scalable and Privacy-Preserving Federated Principal Component Analysis
authors: Froelicher, David; Cho, Hyunghoon; Edupalli, Manaswitha; Sa Sousa, Joao; Bossuat, Jean-Philippe; Pyrgelis, Apostolos; Troncoso-Pastoriza, Juan R.; Berger, Bonnie; Hubaux, Jean-Pierre
venue: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP)
summary: Describes SF-PCA, a federated PCA using multiparty homomorphic encryption that returns results as accurate as centralised PCA irrespective of how data are split, and is 3 to 250 times faster than purely cryptographic alternatives. Relevant to a shared basis when centres do not wish to reveal covariance sums.
note: Preprint arXiv 2304.00129; IEEE S&P 2023 per Crossref.

title: Federated horizontally partitioned principal component analysis for biomedical applications
authors: Hartebrodt, Anne; Röttger, Richard
summary: Examines federated horizontally partitioned PCA for biomedical data and the effects of batch effects and population differences between sites on it. Relevant because sites in a histology federation differ in stain and cohort.
note: Only the abstract was read.

title: Learning from electronic health records across multiple sites: A communication-efficient and privacy-preserving distributed algorithm
authors: Duan, Rui; Boland, Mary Regina; Liu, Zixuan; Liu, Yue; Chang, Howard H; Xu, Hua; Chu, Haitao; Schmid, Christopher H; Forrest, Christopher B; Holmes, John H; Schuemie, Martijn J; Berlin, Jesse A; Moore, Jason H; Chen, Yong
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association 27(3)
summary: Proposes ODAL, a one-shot logistic regression that combines patient data at a lead site with first- and second-order gradients from other sites. In simulation the relative bias against pooled estimates is below 3% (first order) and below 0.1% (second order); in 100 medication analyses, bias was under 10% for 85% and 99% of medications.
note: Seed 'Duan and colleagues 2020' (JAMIA 27(3):376-385). Only the abstract text was retrieved (PMC copy was an abstract-sized file), so read level is abstract only.

title: ODAL: A one-shot distributed algorithm to perform logistic regressions on electronic health records data from multiple clinical sites.
authors: Duan, Rui; Boland, Mary Regina; Moore, Jason H; Chen, Yong
venue: Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing. Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing
summary: Earlier conference version of ODAL, a one-shot, privacy-preserving distributed logistic regression across clinical sites without iterative communication. Reports performance comparable to pooled analysis in simulation.
note: Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing 2019 (proceedings year per PubMed record); abstract only.

title: Heterogeneity-aware and communication-efficient distributed statistical inference
authors: Duan, Rui; Ning, Yang; Chen, Yong
summary: Extends the surrogate-likelihood approach to sites whose covariate distributions and parameters differ (heterogeneity-aware), requiring only aggregated information and few communication rounds. Provides valid inference for the shared parameters.
note: Preprint arXiv 1912.09623; Biometrika 109(1), 2022 (online 2021). Abstract only.

title: DLMM as a lossless one-shot algorithm for collaborative multi-site distributed linear mixed models.
authors: Luo, Chongliang; Islam, Md Nazmul; Sheils, Natalie E; Buresh, John; Reps, Jenna; Schuemie, Martijn J; Ryan, Patrick B; Edmondson, Mackenzie; Duan, Rui; Tong, Jiayi; Marks-Anglin, Arielle; Bian, Jiang; Chen, Zhaoyi; Duarte-Salles, Talita; Fernández-Bertolín, Sergio; et al.
summary: Gives a one-shot algorithm for linear mixed models with site-specific random effects in which each site sends cross-product summaries and the pooled likelihood is reconstructed exactly, so effect sizes and standard errors equal those from pooled data. Demonstrated on COVID-19 length of stay: 538 hospitals in one insurer database and 120,609 patients from 11 data sources.
note: Full text retrieved (Nature Communications, open access) and read: abstract, discussion and figure legends. Closest published match to the federated mixed-model route with centre as random effect.

title: dPQL: a lossless distributed algorithm for generalized linear mixed model with application to privacy-preserving hospital profiling
authors: Luo, Chongliang; Islam, Md Nazmul; Sheils, Natalie E; Buresh, John; Schuemie, Martijn J; Doshi, Jalpa A; Werner, Rachel M; Asch, David A; Chen, Yong
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association
summary: Provides a lossless distributed algorithm for generalised linear mixed models applied to hospital profiling, matching pooled-data fits. Extends the exact-reconstruction idea from the linear to the generalised linear case.
note: Abstract only.

title: Linear Mixed Modeling of Federated Data When Only the Mean, Covariance, and Sample Size Are Available.
authors: Limpoco, Marie Analiz April; Faes, Christel; Hens, Niel
summary: Shows that a linear mixed model can be fitted exactly from each provider's sample size, mean vector and covariance matrix, sent once, by the principle of sufficiency. Demonstrated on 15,068 records from 70 clinics.
note: Statistics in Medicine 2025 (PubMed record); the arXiv version 2407.20796 was retrieved and its abstract and conclusion read. The input summary (means, covariance, n) matches the sums already held by the project.

title: FedGMMAT: Federated generalized linear mixed model association tests.
authors: Li, Wentao; Chen, Han; Jiang, Xiaoqian; Harmanci, Arif
summary: Develops federated generalised linear mixed model association tests for genetic data across institutions. Relevant as an application of federated random-effect models in genomics.
note: Abstract only.

title: Federated generalized linear mixed models for collaborative genome-wide association studies.
authors: Li, Wentao; Chen, Han; Jiang, Xiaoqian; Harmanci, Arif
summary: Federated GLMM-based GWAS addressing population stratification and confounding while protecting privacy through shared intermediate statistics. Shows federated mixed models in genomics.
note: Abstract only.

title: Federated learning algorithms for generalized mixed-effects model (GLMM) on horizontally partitioned data from distributed sources.
authors: Li, Wentao; Tong, Jiayi; Anjum, Md Monowar; Mohammed, Noman; Chen, Yong; Jiang, Xiaoqian
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
summary: Develops two approximate federated algorithms for generalised mixed-effects models and compares them with a centralised lme4 fit, with fixes for numerical error and singularity. Shows that approximate federated GLMMs can approach centralised results but need care.
note: Abstract only.

title: Multisite learning of high-dimensional heterogeneous data with applications to opioid use disorder study of 15,000 patients across 5 clinical sites
authors: Liu, Xiaokang; Duan, Rui; Luo, Chongliang; Ogdie, Alexis; Moore, Jason H.; Kranzler, Henry R.; Bian, Jiang; Chen, Yong
summary: One-shot, summary-statistics-based distributed algorithm (ADAP) for penalised regression across datasets, using gradient information from collaborators at a lead site. Applied to an opioid use disorder study of about 15,000 patients across 5 sites.
note: Abstract only.

title: ODACH: a one-shot distributed algorithm for Cox model with heterogeneous multi-center data
authors: Luo, Chongliang; Duan, Rui; Naj, Adam C.; Kranzler, Henry R.; Bian, Jiang; Chen, Yong
summary: One-shot distributed Cox model with site-specific baseline hazards (ODACH); simulation and an opioid use disorder study show estimates closer to pooled analysis than meta-analysis, notably for rare events. Illustrates how a one-shot method can beat naive meta-analysis.
note: Abstract only; web-result text also seen.

title: PDA (Privacy-Preserving Distributed Algorithms) in action: ten principles for high-quality multi-site clinical evidence generation
authors: Chen, Yong; Tong, Jiayi; Lu, Yiwen; Duan, Rui; Luo, Chongliang; Suchard, Marc A; Ryan, Patrick B; Williams, Andrew E; Holmes, John H; Moore, Jason H; Xu, Hua; Lu, Yun; Carroll, Raymond J; Zeger, Scott L; Hripcsak, George; et al.
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association
summary: Sets out ten principles for high-quality multi-site analyses with privacy-preserving distributed algorithms (PDA). A recent statement of practice from the group behind ODAL and DLMM.
note: 2026 article; abstract only.

title: Unlocking multi-institutional insights into disease progression with PEAL as a lossless, one-shot federated learning solution
authors: Shen, Yicheng; Kim, Ji Soo; Luo, Chongliang; Zeger, Scott L.; Domsic, Robyn T.; Shah, Ami A.; Tong, Jiayi
summary: Introduces PEAL, a lossless one-shot federated method for longitudinal multi-site EHR data that handles site heterogeneity. Shows the one-shot, lossless line extended to repeated measures.
note: 2026; abstract only.

title: COLA-GLM: collaborative one-shot and lossless algorithms of generalized linear models for decentralized observational healthcare data
authors: Wu, Qiong; Reps, Jenna M.; Li, Lu; Zhang, Bingyu; Lu, Yiwen; Tong, Jiayi; Zhang, Dazheng; Lumley, Thomas; Brand, Milou T.; Van Zandt, Mui; Falconer, Thomas; He, Xing; Huang, Yu; Li, Haoyang; Yan, Chao; et al.
summary: Presents COLA-GLM, one-shot lossless algorithms for generalised linear models with heterogeneity across sites. Another application of the summary-statistics approach.
note: Abstract only.

title: A one-shot, lossless algorithm for cross-cohort learning in mixed-outcomes analysis
authors: Li, Ruowang; Benz, Luke; Duan, Rui; Denny, Joshua C.; Hakonarson, Hakon; Mosley, Jonathan D.; Smoller, Jordan W.; Wei, Wei-Qi; Lumley, Thomas; Ritchie, Marylyn D.; Moore, Jason H.; Chen, Yong
summary: mixWAS is a one-shot, lossless algorithm for mixed-outcome analysis across cohorts that avoids pooling or harmonisation. Included as a recent example of lossless one-shot methods.
note: Abstract only.

title: Distributed Statistical Analyses: A Scoping Review and Examples of Operational Frameworks Adapted to Health Analytics
authors: Camirand Lemyre, Félix; Lévesque, Simon; Domingue, Marie-Pier; Herrmann, Klaus; Ethier, Jean-François
summary: Scoping review of distributed statistical analysis methods and operational frameworks for health data networks. A survey of which analyses can be run without pooling.
note: Abstract only.

title: Federated and distributed learning applications for electronic health records and structured medical data: A scoping review
authors: Li, Siqi; Liu, Pinyan; Nascimento, Gustavo G.; Wang, Xinru; Leite, Fabio Renato Manzolli; Chakraborty, Bibhas; Hong, Chuan; Ning, Yilin; Xie, Feng; Teo, Zhen Ling; Ting, Daniel Shu Wei; Haddadi, Hamed; Ong, Marcus Eng Hock; Peres, Marco Aurélio; Liu, Nan
summary: Scoping review of federated and distributed learning applications to electronic health records and structured data. Maps what has been done on non-image clinical data.
note: Abstract only.

title: A review of distributed statistical inference
authors: Gao, Yuan; Liu, Weidong; Wang, Hansheng; Wang, Xiaozhou; Yan, Yibo; Zhang, Riquan
summary: Review of distributed statistical inference covering one-shot and iterative approaches for parametric and nonparametric models. Provides a map of the theory that the project's candidate methods come from.
note: Published in Statistical Theory and Related Fields 2022 per a tandfonline page seen in a web result (not opened by this agent); listed here as the preprint.

title: DataSHIELD: taking the analysis to the data, not the data to the analysis
authors: Gaye, Amadou; Marcon, Yannick; Isaeva, Julia; LaFlamme, Philippe; Turner, Andrew; Jones, Elinor M; Minion, Joel; Boyd, Andrew W; Newby, Christopher J; Nuotio, Marja-Liisa; Wilson, Rebecca; Butters, Oliver; Murtagh, Barnaby; Demir, Ipek; Doiron, Dany; et al.
summary: Describes the DataSHIELD platform: analysis commands go to each site's data computer and only non-disclosive summaries return. The article states, citing earlier work, that GLMs fitted this way are exactly the pooled fit and shows this on example data.
note: Seed 'Gaye et al. 2014'. Full text retrieved and read (abstract, discussion, targeted passages).

title: Orchestrating privacy-protected big data analyses of data from different resources with R and DataSHIELD
authors: Marcon, Yannick; Bishop, Tom; Avraam, Demetris; Escriba-Montagut, Xavier; Ryser-Welch, Patricia; Wheater, Stuart; Burton, Paul; González, Juan R.
summary: Describes the DataSHIELD platform's R packages and how they support federated analysis with disclosure control, and how it can be extended to other R packages. Documents practice in epidemiological consortia.

title: DataSHIELD: mitigating disclosure risk in a multi-site federated analysis platform
authors: Avraam, Demetris; Wilson, Rebecca C; Aguirre Chan, Noemi; Banerjee, Soumya; Bishop, Tom R P; Butters, Olly; Cadman, Tim; Cederkvist, Luise; Duijts, Liesbeth; Escribà Montagut, Xavier; Garner, Hugh; Gonçalves, Gonçalo; González, Juan R; Haakma, Sido; Hartlev, Mette; et al.

note: Abstract only; year taken from the EUR page (2025).

title: MOLGENIS Armadillo: a lightweight server for federated analysis using DataSHIELD
authors: Cadman, Tim; Slofstra, Mariska K; van der Geest, Marije A; Avraam, Demetris; Bishop, Tom R P; de Boer, Tommy; Duijts, Liesbeth; Haakma, Sido; Hyde, Eleanor; Jaddoe, Vincent; Karramass, Tarik; Kelpin, Fleur; Marcon, Yannick; Pinot de Moira, Angela; Postma, Dick; et al.
summary: Presents MOLGENIS Armadillo, a lightweight DataSHIELD server for cohort consortia. Shows the barrier for a data holder is a server install rather than model training.
note: Abstract only; Bioinformatics 41(1), 2025.

title: Capability and accuracy of usual statistical analyses in a real-world setting using a federated approach
authors: Jégou, Romain; Bachot, Camille; Monteil, Charles; Boernert, Eric; Chmiel, Jacek; Boucher, Mathieu; Pau, David
summary: Tests whether DataSHIELD reproduces classical centralised analyses on a synthetic oncology cohort split across three simulated sites. Compares federated against pooled output for usual statistical analyses.
note: Abstract only.

title: On the relative efficiency of using summary statistics versus individual-level data in meta-analysis
authors: Lin, D. Y.; Zeng, D.
summary: Proves that for common parametric and semiparametric models there is no asymptotic efficiency loss in combining maximum-likelihood summary statistics compared with analysing individual-level data when the main parameter is shared. Also examines cases with differing parameters or shared nuisance parameters.
note: Full text retrieved (UNC repository PDF) and abstract and conclusion region checked; the extracted tail was references, so the discussion text was not closely read.

title: Multivariate Meta-Analysis of Heterogeneous Studies Using Only Summary Statistics: Efficiency and Robustness
authors: Liu, Dungang; Liu, Regina Y.; Xie, Minge
venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
summary: Develops multivariate meta-analysis for heterogeneous studies using only summary statistics and shows efficiency close to that of individual-level analysis. Relevant for combining sites that do not share all parameters.
note: Abstract only.

title: Relative efficiency of using summary versus individual data in random-effects meta-analysis.
authors: Chen, Ding-Geng; Liu, Dungang; Min, Xiaoyi; Zhang, Heping
summary: Shows that, with Gaussian random effects and maximum-likelihood summaries, summary-statistics meta-analysis is at most as efficient as individual-level analysis and asymptotically equivalent when both study size and number of studies are large. With small or moderate studies and numbers, summary-level analysis can lose efficiency appreciably.
note: Condition relevant for few centres.

title: Meta-analysis using individual participant data: one-stage and two-stage approaches, and why they may differ
authors: Burke, Danielle L.; Ensor, Joie; Riley, Richard D.
summary: Explains why one-stage and two-stage individual participant data meta-analyses can differ (exact versus approximate likelihoods, weighting, within- versus across-trial information). Gives the conditions under which they agree.
note: Abstract only.

title: Targeting underrepresented populations in precision medicine: A federated transfer learning approach
authors: Li, Sai; Cai, Tianxi; Duan, Rui
summary: Proposes FETA, a federated transfer learning method that borrows information from source populations and sites to improve a model for an under-represented target population. Reports performance comparable to pooled analysis with few communication rounds and better prediction than target-only, source-only or naive pooled models in the eMERGE application.
note: Seed 'Li, Cai and Duan 2023' (Ann Appl Stat 17(4):2970-2992, DOI 10.1214/23-AOAS1747). Full text retrieved (arXiv 2108.12112 and journal version); abstract and discussion read. eMERGE application: 55,029 subjects from ten sites; target analysis uses 20,247 samples from seven sites.

title: Transfer Learning for High-Dimensional Linear Regression: Prediction, Estimation and Minimax Optimality
authors: Li, Sai; Cai, T. Tony; Li, Hongzhe
venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B: Statistical Methodology
summary: Gives estimators and minimax rates for high-dimensional linear regression that borrows from related auxiliary studies, with a step that selects informative sources. Foundational statistical theory for the transfer learning in FETA.
note: J R Stat Soc B 84(1), 2022 (online 2021). Abstract only.

title: Transfer Learning Under High-Dimensional Generalized Linear Models
authors: Tian, Ye; Feng, Yang
venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
summary: Extends transfer learning to high-dimensional GLMs with error bounds and a source-detection step. Gives the GLM version of the above.
note: Abstract only.

title: Federated Transfer Learning with Differential Privacy
authors: Li, Mengchu; Tian, Ye; Feng, Yang; Yu, Yi
summary: Studies federated transfer learning under differential privacy and site heterogeneity, with theory for a target dataset aided by several sources. Brings privacy cost into the statistical framework.
note: Preprint; abstract only.

title: Enhancing Genetic Risk Prediction through Federated Semi-Supervised Transfer Learning with Inaccurate Electronic Health Record Data.
authors: Lu, Yuying; Gu, Tian; Duan, Rui
summary: Federated semi-supervised transfer learning for genetic risk prediction from EHR with inaccurate labels and demographic imbalance. Example of federated transfer under noisy labels.
note: Abstract only.

title: ReFIT: Federated Transfer Learning for Sequential Prediction and Uncertainty Quantification Using Streaming EHR Data
authors: Lu, Yuying; Luo, Lan; Gu, Tian
summary: ReFIT combines federated transfer learning with renewable estimation for sequentially arriving source data and gives conformal prediction intervals that narrow as sources accumulate while coverage holds. Relevant to uncertainty with growing federation size.
note: 2026; abstract and a web-result passage read; PMC13344382 exists.

title: Federated Machine Learning: Concept and Applications
authors: Yang, Qiang; Liu, Yang; Chen, Tianjian; Tong, Yongxin
summary: Frames secure federated learning as horizontal, vertical and federated transfer learning and sets out the concept. Standard reference for the taxonomy.
note: Preprint; Yang et al. 2019 (ACM TIST version not opened).

title: Federated causal inference in heterogeneous observational data
authors: Xiong, Ruoxuan; Koenecke, Allison; Powell, Michael; Shen, Zhu; Vogelstein, Joshua T.; Athey, Susan
summary: Gives federated estimators and variances for average treatment effects from site-level summaries across heterogeneous sites, with asymptotic equivalence to pooled analysis and valid confidence intervals. Shows that valid uncertainty can be obtained from summary information.
note: Stat Med 42(24), 2023; preprint arXiv 2107.11732 (abstract page seen). Abstract only.

title: Robust Inference for Federated Meta-Learning
authors: Guo, Zijian; Li, Xiudi; Han, Larry; Cai, Tianxi
summary: Proposes robust inference for federated meta-learning that adjusts confidence intervals for the uncertainty in selecting which sites are eligible. Addresses inference when some sites differ from the prevailing model.
note: Preprint; a PMC copy (PMC12266688) exists indicating later publication, venue not verified. Abstract only.

title: Federated Conformal Predictors for Distributed Uncertainty Quantification
authors: Lu, Charles; Yu, Yaodong; Karimireddy, Sai Praneeth; Jordan, Michael I.; Raskar, Ramesh
summary: Extends conformal prediction to federated learning where client heterogeneity violates exchangeability, and gives prediction sets with coverage under a shared-quantile construction. Relevant to valid uncertainty in a federation.
note: ICML 2023 per arXiv comment. Abstract only; a conformal theme is probably covered by another fragment.

title: Bayesian federated inference for survival models.
authors: Pazira, Hassan; Massa, Emanuele; Weijers, Jetty A M; Coolen, Anthony C C; Jonker, Marianne A
summary: Bayesian federated inference for survival models: combines per-centre estimates into a joint estimator with approximate credible intervals, and treats heterogeneity of baseline hazards. Illustrates inference from summaries with heterogeneity.
note: J Appl Stat 2026; PMC12872092 page seen. Abstract only.

title: One-Shot Federated Learning
authors: Guha, Neel; Talwalkar, Ameet; Smith, Virginia
venue: arXiv preprint (workshop paper per arXiv comment)
summary: One-shot federated learning where a server learns a global model in a single round through ensembling and knowledge aggregation; reaches about 90% of the unattainable global ideal and a 51.5% average relative AUC gain over local baselines. Early reference for the one-round idea.
note: Workshop paper (arXiv comment). Abstract only.

title: Parametric Feature Transfer: One-shot Federated Learning with Foundation Models
authors: Beitollahi, Mahdi; Bie, Alex; Hemati, Sobhan; Brunswic, Leo Maxime; Li, Xu; Chen, Xi; Zhang, Guojun
summary: FedPFT has each client fit Gaussian mixtures to features from a frozen foundation model and send them; the server samples synthetic features to train a classifier head in one round. Reports improvements up to 20.6% in the communication-accuracy tradeoff over other one-shot methods on eight datasets, plus differential-privacy variants and reconstruction attacks that succeed when real features are sent.
note: Full text retrieved; abstract and conclusion read. Classification of natural images; the later TMLR version (Beitollahi et al. 2025, 'Foundation models meet federated learning: a one-shot feature-sharing method') is known to this agent only from a reference list in another paper (secondary).

title: Accelerating Heterogeneous Federated Learning with Closed-form Classifiers
authors: Fanì, Eros; Camoriano, Raffaello; Caputo, Barbara; Ciccone, Marco
summary: Fed3R fits a closed-form ridge classifier on pre-trained features by aggregating client sufficient statistics, making it immune to label heterogeneity and independent of client order. Requires up to two orders of magnitude less communication and computation than competitors and improves accuracy by up to 12% in hard cross-device cases.
note: ICML 2024 per arXiv comment. Full text retrieved; abstract and conclusion read. Image classification, not regression on expression.

title: AFL: A Single-Round Analytic Approach for Federated Learning with Pre-trained Models
authors: He, Run; Tong, Kai; Fang, Di; Sun, Han; Zeng, Ziqian; Li, Haoran; Chen, Tianyi; Zhuang, Huiping
summary: Analytic federated learning solves a local least-squares problem on frozen-encoder embeddings and combines client solutions in one round with an aggregation law, so the result is identical for any partition of the data across clients. Experiments, including extremely non-IID splits and 1000 or more clients, show competitive accuracy.
note: CVPR 2025 per arXiv comment. Full text retrieved; abstract, method summary and conclusion read. Classification, with the head being a linear regression onto one-hot labels. Its appendix shows the aggregation without a regularisation step drifts from the joint solution (deviation about 1 at 20 clients and about 1e12 at 200) while the regularised version stays near 1e-10; numerical conditioning matters for exactness.

title: Covariances for Free: Exploiting Mean Distributions for Training-free Federated Learning
authors: Goswami, Dipam; Magistri, Simone; Wang, Kai; Twardowski, Bartłomiej; Bagdanov, Andrew D.; van de Weijer, Joost
summary: FedCOF estimates class covariances from only the class means the clients send, using an unbiased estimator, and uses them to initialise a classifier, with 4-26% gain over mean-only methods at equal communication. Competitive with methods that send second-order statistics, and outperforms federated prompt tuning.
note: NeurIPS 2025 per arXiv comment. Full text retrieved; abstract and conclusion read. On a six-client DomainNet feature-shift test, Fed3R scored 81.9 and FedCOF 74.1 with far less communication (0.3 vs 39.6 MB).

title: One-Shot Federated Ridge Regression: Exact Recovery via Sufficient Statistic Aggregation
authors: Alsulaimawi, Zahir
summary: Shows that federated ridge regression can be solved in one round by summing client Gram matrices and moment vectors, matching the centralised solution exactly when a coverage condition holds. Adds random-projection compression, one-time differential-privacy noise and client-dropout handling, with simulations reporting 10-80 fold less communication than FedAvg. All reported experiments use synthetic data (20 clients, 500 samples each, 100 features).
note: Single-author 2026 arXiv preprint, not peer-reviewed. Full text retrieved; abstract, scope statement and conclusion read. The exact recovery is elementary algebra (as the paper itself says); the value is in the privacy and compression extensions. Linear models only.
